headline: Would have required the VA to study how cannabis affects veterans with PTSD or chronic pain; the Senate did not take it up.
what_it_does: The bill would have required the Department of Veterans Affairs to run an 18-month observational study on how cannabis affects the health of certain veterans. If the VA found it could meet the needed standards, it would then have had to run clinical trials using cannabis approved for research by the Food and Drug Administration, followed by a long-term study of trial participants. The VA could have stopped the trials if it could not meet clinical guidelines or if they posed too much risk to participants. Study groups would have had to reflect the makeup of US veterans based on Census data, and participant data would have been kept anonymous.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans enrolled in VA health care who have PTSD or chronic pain
who_it_affects.how: They would have been eligible to take part in VA studies and clinical trials on cannabis.
The VA would have been required to carry out the studies and trials and report on whether it could meet the standards for clinical trials.
The FDA would have determined which cannabis was appropriate for research use in the VA trials.
